figures.caption: Figure 1: Multi-sample aggregation paradigms. A group of g trials elicited by the same stimulus passes through a shared CNN backbone. The paradigms compared in this paper differ in where along the pipeline aggregation across trials occurs: at the input (prior work), at intermediate features via learned attention or weighting (ours), at the logits during training (ours), or after softmax at evaluation time (prior work).

Table 1: Test balanced accuracy across three primary aggregation paradigms and seven (dataset, task, group size) conditions. Values are mean ± standard deviation across 5 random seeds. The best mean in each row is shown in bold. Significance markers indicate paired t-tests against input averaging: ∗ for p < 0.05, ∗∗ for p < 0.01. Results for the three additional aggregation methods we evaluate are reported in Appendix E.

Table 5: Test balanced accuracy of the three attention-based aggregation methods across all seven (dataset, task, group size) conditions. LWA: learned weighted averaging. CTA: cross-trial attention. LQA: learned query attention. Values are mean ± standard deviation across 5 random seeds. Significance markers indicate paired t-tests against input averaging: ∗ for p < 0.05, ∗∗ for p < 0.01.

Table 6: Per-class performance on phoneme classification, broken out by training-frequency tertile. The best value in each (metric, g, tertile) cell is shown in bold. p̄true denotes the mean predicted probability assigned to the true class. †The low-frequency tertile at g=100 contains only 3 of the 13 classes assigned to the bucket; the remaining 10 have insufficient test samples to form complete groups and are excluded. Values are means over 5 seeds.
Table 9: Per-decile balanced accuracy for group-level predictions (g = 10), ranked by group-level confidence (decile 1: most confident; decile 10: least confident). Values are means across 5 seeds.
